    guests = sorted(guests)

def format_dates(date_str):
    match = re.search(r"(January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+(\d+),\s+(\d{4})", date_str)
    if not match:

    day = match.group(2)
    year = match.group(3)

from datetime import timedelta

def rotate_logs(log_directory):
    for log in get_new_logs(log_directory):
        backup_file = create_backup(log)
        compress(backup_file)
        remove_from_archive(log)

def get_new_logs(directory):

def create_backup(log_file):
    backup_dir = '/var/backups'

    shutil.copy2(log_file, backup_dir)
    backup_file = os.path.join(backup_dir, os.path.basename(log_file))
    os.chmod(backup_file, 0o755)
    return backup_file

def compress(backup_file):
    tar_path = backup_file + '.tar.gz'

This device delivers air directly into your lungs for breathing underwater - but it requires special skills and training to use safely.

Professional divers have the knowledge, experience, physical conditioning, safety procedures, etc needed for working with scuba gear in the ocean or other aquatic environments. Without this extensive training, attempting to scuba dive will likely result in serious accidents or fatalities due to respiratory failure, decompression sickness, drowning, trauma from contact with sharp objects in the murky water, running out of gas while underwater, becoming separated from the dive team, etc.

The only way to dive properly and responsibly is to enroll in a reputable dive center that teaches certified courses leading to a qualification like CCR Open Water Diver, PADI Scuba Instructor, NAUI Advanced Scuba Certificate, SSI Pro Course, etc. These programs take years to complete, involve hundreds of hours in dry land classes plus actual open water dives with trained instructors to demonstrate competency and mastery. Only after passing written exams, written assignments, logbook requirements, underwater skill tests and safety evaluations will new recruits be granted entry-level access. Afterward, advanced certification can build even more expertise through progressively deeper and faster dives as well as specialized techniques.

So while many people do start going diving right away after completing basic training, it's important to recognize there's a lot of practice, study and real-world application taking place to prepare you.     tar_file = tarfile.open(tar_path)
    with tar_file as tar:
        temp_extract_path = tar.gettempdir() / tar.getmembers()
        tar.extractall(path=temp_extract_path)

            if not extracted_member.exists():

            extracted_member.unlink()

            new_member = parent / (member.name + '.new')

The concept of imaginary numbers is quite simple but often misunderstood.

A complex number z can be written as a + bi where a and b are real numbers and i represents the square root of -1

The key insight here is that there exists some value for square root of negative 1 that makes this true. We refer to this new unit as "i" which turns out to behave like a rotation operation in mathematics.

The imaginary part b in z = a + bi measures how far you'd have rotated counterclockwise if doing just the rotational component without affecting x at all.

So while there's no actual quantity represented directly by an imaginary number, it can act as a powerful placeholder in algebraic manipulations involving such quantities as solutions to quadratic equations with negative discriminants or to express rotations or waves succinctly. Sharks belong to an ancient group of fish called chondrichthyans that evolved over hundreds of millions of years before dinosaurs or mammals ever existed on Earth. Unlike most animals whose skeletons are made up of hard mineralized bones, sharks have cartilaginous skeletons instead.


Cartilage is a tough tissue that's found throughout your body - for example in your ears, nose, and fingers - it gives structure without being as brittle as other types of bone. A chondritic skeleton means the shark's skeleton is all made out of this cartilage material.

This gives sharks several advantages as compared with most vertebrates:
- A lightweight but strong skeleton allows them to swim more efficiently 
- Their cartilage can absorb impacts when diving deeper into the ocean
- Shark skin has ridges that make them less slippery

However unlike you, sharks don't heal their bones like other animals - if you cut into a shark, its cartilage cells will die and remain like this until the shark dies itself!

Even though sharks aren't mammals or birds with backbones like we have, many people use terms like "fish" to describe them due to similarities like fins and scales which actually evolved independently in multiple lineages of aquatic animals.

import tarfile
import os

def extract_archive(archive_path):
    with tarfile.open(archive_path) as tf:
        temp_dir = 'tmp'
        os.makedirs(temp_dir)

        def is_within_directory(directory, target):
            abs_directory = os.path.abspath(directory)
            abs_target = os.path.abspath(target)
            prefix = os.path.commonprefix([abs_directory, abs_target])
            return prefix == abs_directory

        def on_extract(path):
            if not is_within_directory(temp_dir, path):
                raise Exception(f'Attempted to extract archive entry {path} outside of base directory')

        tf.extractall(members=filter(on_extract, tf.getmembers()), path=temp_dir)

extract_archive('data.tar')
